name: T-VEC (talimogene laherparepvec)
cyclesNote: Intralesional oncolytic immunotherapy for injectable cutaneous, subcutaneous, and nodal melanoma lesions (unresectable stage IIIB to IVM1a in-transit / satellite disease). First injection at the lower concentration; a second injection follows about 3 weeks later, then injections continue at the higher concentration every 2 weeks for at least 6 months, and beyond that until no injectable lesions remain, complete response, disease progression requiring another therapy, or unacceptable toxicity.

institution.provenance: ONCQIS grounded Standard Protocol (experimental, owner/device test only; not clinically activated)

biomarkers.note: Genetically modified herpes-simplex-1 oncolytic immunotherapy expressing GM-CSF, injected directly into accessible melanoma lesions for local and locoregional control. No companion biomarker is required and it is used regardless of BRAF status. Selection is anatomic (injectable in-transit / satellite / nodal disease) rather than molecular.

supportiveCare: Herpetic precautions: cover injection sites with an occlusive dressing; caregivers and clinicians handling the product should use gloves and eye protection; avoid direct contact for immunosuppressed or pregnant household contacts.
Aciclovir or other anti-herpetic agents can reduce T-VEC efficacy; if a herpetic infection is treated, note the potential interaction.
Manage common flu-like symptoms (fever, chills, fatigue) and injection-site pain symptomatically.
monitoring: clinical assessment of injected and non-injected lesions for local and locoregional response before each injection
review for herpetic lesions in the patient and close contacts

doseModificationRules.condition: no remaining injectable lesions but not yet complete response
doseModificationRules.text: Continue therapy for at least 6 months; if all injectable lesions have resolved, hold and reassess, resuming if new injectable lesions appear. Physician decides.

drugs.name: Talimogene laherparepvec (T-VEC)
drugs.notes: Intralesional (intratumoral) injection, total volume up to 4 mL per treatment distributed across lesions by lesion size. First dose at 10^6 (1 million) PFU/mL. Second dose about 3 weeks later, and all subsequent doses every 2 weeks, at 10^8 (100 million) PFU/mL. Volume per lesion is size-directed (roughly: >5 cm up to 4 mL; 2.5 to 5 cm up to 2 mL; 1.5 to 2.5 cm up to 1 mL; 0.5 to 1.5 cm up to 0.5 mL; <0.5 cm up to 0.1 mL). Dose here is expressed as maximum injected volume, not a body-size calculation; the concentration and per-lesion volume are the operative parameters. Own-wording summary of standard prescribing; not a verbatim label copy.
